skill.name: svg-logo-generator
skill.description: Generate high-quality, minimalistic, and geometric SVG logos using Python scripts. Use this skill when users need to create logos, icons, or visual identities with geometric primitives (circles, rects, paths) and specific color schemes. Applies generative design principles with standardized workflows for scalable SVG output.
skill.summary: Guides AI assistants to create scalable geometric SVG logos with self-contained Python scripts.
skill.author: Dwsy

security_audit.summary: Static command execution alerts are Markdown formatting and a fenced Python example, not executable Ruby or shell syntax. The only file write is a hardcoded logo.svg output path for the intended SVG workflow, with no prompt injection evidence found.

static_findings.snippet: - **Constraint**: Do NOT rely on external non-standard libraries (like `cairo` or `svgwrite`). Use s
- **Scalability**: Always use `viewBox` instead of fixed `width/height` alone

finding_verdicts.reason: The snippet is Markdown inline code naming the SVG viewBox attribute. It does not execute Ruby or shell code.

The backticks only format the filename logo.svg in documentation. The line is an expected output instruction, not shell syntax.
The matched text is the opening Markdown fence for a Python example. The enclosed example uses normal SVG string assembly and file output, not Ruby backtick execution.
The matched text is the closing Markdown fence and adjacent prose. It is not executable code and contains no shell command.

The Python example writes a hardcoded logo.svg file as the advertised output. There is no user-controlled path, path traversal, or secret file access.

content.value_statement: Teams need scalable logos without heavy design tooling. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to generate clean SVG logos with Python.
actual_capabilities: Guides visual metaphor, color palette, and geometric composition planning.
Defines a scalable SVG canvas with a viewBox and XML namespace.
Uses Python standard library methods for SVG string generation.
Provides a sample workflow that writes a logo.svg file.
Focuses on circles, rectangles, paths, polygons, and hex colors.
limitations: It does not create raster images or interactive design previews.
It does not perform trademark, copyright, or brand clearance checks.
Complex illustrative logos may need manual refinement after generation.
The sample workflow writes one logo.svg file unless modified.

use_cases.title: Prototype a Startup Mark
use_cases.description: Create a simple SVG logo concept before investing in a full brand system.

use_cases.title: Generate Product Icons
use_cases.description: Build geometric icons that share a consistent canvas, palette, and visual style.

use_cases.title: Automate SVG Asset Creation
use_cases.description: Produce lightweight logo files with Python for documentation, demos, or internal tools.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Logo Concept
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one simple logo.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a minimal SVG logo for a coffee app. Use two colors, simple geometry, and save it as logo.svg.

prompt_templates.title: Responsive Product Icon
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request with canvas and palette details.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a geometric SVG icon for a finance dashboard. Use a 512 by 512 canvas, a viewBox, and a blue and green palette.

prompt_templates.title: Logo System Directions
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for multiple related concepts.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a logo system for an AI developer tool. Provide primary, secondary, and monochrome SVG concepts with consistent geometry.

prompt_templates.title: Parameterized SVG Generator
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for a reusable generation workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a Python-generated SVG logo for a security analytics product. Use layered paths, reusable style variables, and explain the design choices briefly.

output_examples.input: Create a minimal SVG logo for a task planner with a blue and yellow palette.
output_examples.output: A clean geometric mark using a 512 canvas, a centered check shape, balanced spacing, and a logo.svg output plan.

output_examples.input: Design three logo directions for a developer documentation site.
output_examples.output: Three SVG logo concepts with distinct metaphors, shared proportions, and concise notes about shape choices.

output_examples.input: Generate an icon-style logo for a data visualization tool.
output_examples.output: A scalable SVG concept using simple chart-inspired geometry, consistent hex colors, and editable shape structure.

best_practices: Provide the brand name, audience, colors, and shape preferences before generation.
Ask for a viewBox-based SVG so the asset scales cleanly.
Review the generated mark at small and large sizes before final use.
anti_patterns: Do not request complex photorealistic artwork from a simple SVG geometry workflow.
Do not omit the desired palette, brand tone, or target audience.
Do not depend on non-standard Python packages unless the user approves them.

faq.question: Does this skill create raster images?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on scalable SVG logos and Python scripts that write SVG files.

faq.question: Can it use my brand colors?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide hex colors, contrast requirements, and any colors to avoid.

faq.question: Does it require external libraries?
faq.answer: No. The workflow recommends Python standard library tools or formatted SVG strings.

faq.question: Can Codex use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Will it check trademarks?
faq.answer: No. It does not perform trademark, copyright, or brand clearance checks.

faq.question: Can it create multiple concepts?
faq.answer: Yes. Ask for several geometric directions, then refine the strongest option.
